data.why: app.py fetches ATP match CSVs and Match Charting Project point data from raw.githubusercontent.com at runtime (no bundled data), but the sandboxed server has no network once running, so synthetic CSVs matching the exact expected schema are seeded locally and a thin launcher monkeypatches the CSV-fetch function to read them instead.

goals: Determine whether physiological-load (rolling court-time) features add predictive lift over ranking alone, using the Ablation Study tab's staged AUC comparison
Benchmark the calibrated Gradient Boosting pre-match model's accuracy, ROC-AUC, Brier score, and reliability diagram against naive baselines (Higher-Rank-Wins, Rank-Only Logistic, Elo-style)
Inspect feature importances to see which cascade-stage features (load, form, head-to-head, opponent quality) drive the model's predictions
Run a specific matchup in the Match Inference tab and move the rest-day/load sliders to test fatigue counterfactuals on win probability
Check the in-match score-state model's AUC/Brier and see how its win probability trajectory shifts across sets, games, and server in the In-Match Win Probability tab
Use the leak-check diagnostic (console log of mean feature values by outcome) to confirm pre-match features don't encode the result

review.summary: The tree covers the interface's purpose well (does court-time load add predictive value beyond ranking?), with sensible phases, faithful labels and screens that match. But the second agent's replay confirmed nothing, and the run used real pre-match data instead of the planned synthetic set without explaining why. Fix those, the wrong 'one-of' branches and the startup phase, and add a verdict step before filing.
